method:
WHAT THIS COUNTS. Public posts in which a person describes actually using one of five consumer AI agent products (Instinct, Meta's Muse, Grok Bot, Manus's Cue, OpenAI's dots) for a task. Each included post was read by a coder and tagged with one or more use-case categories from a fixed codebook (taxonomy.json). Counts are of POSTS, not people or usage volume.

SOURCES. X (public search through a logged-out Nitter mirror, keyword queries per product, walked back in 4-day windows), Reddit (public search and subreddit RSS feeds plus thread comments), Hacker News (Algolia search), App Store reviews (Apple's public review feed, which only exposes about the 500 most recent reviews per app), Google Play reviews, and YouTube (video search plus comments; YouTube dates are approximate because they come from relative "x days ago" stamps). Because the Nitter mirror returned few posts for dots and Cue, on 2026-10-08 an additional 71 X posts for those two products (68 dots, 3 Cue) were located with X's own full-archive search and their text was then read from the same public Nitter status pages; this one-off supplement is listed in pipeline/queries/x_supplement_2026-10-08.tsv and is not part of the automated daily run. TikTok and Instagram were probed logged out; both require login to search, so they contribute nothing unless listed below. Posts by platform: X 1188, Reddit 400, Google Play 281, App Store 150, Hacker News 49, YouTube 31, TikTok 19.

HISTORY. Instinct and Muse posts first collected in a sweep on 2026-10-02 (earliest Instinct post found: 2026-08-16; Muse from its 2026-09-08 launch) carry first_seen = 2026-10-02. On 2026-10-08 collection was extended to all five products, going back to each launch date for Grok Bot (2026-08-11), Cue (2026-09-28) and dots (2026-09-29), and re-covering Instinct and Muse from 2026-09-30. Later runs add new posts daily with first_seen = the run date.

CODING RULES. Included: first-hand reports of using the product for something, including concrete first-hand complaints. Excluded: posts by the maker or its staff, sponsored, affiliated or self-promotional posts, relays of someone else's experience or of news, jokes and satire, invite or referral-code templates, entries in contests or sweepstakes run by the maker, launch demos made with early access for a video, posts by people who appear to work for the maker even when that could not be confirmed (marked "affiliation not verified"), speculation by non-users, posts where the product meant is ambiguous (for example "muse" as an ordinary word, or "grok bot" meaning X's @grok reply bot), non-English posts, and repeat posts by the same author about the same experience (coded once). A post can carry several categories. "Saving money on bills & subscriptions" merges two earlier codes (bill negotiation and subscription audits). "General opinion, no use case" and "Testing the agent" are recorded but not ranked. Use-case codes, sentiment and include/exclude decisions are coder judgements. Quotes are verbatim excerpts of at most 280 characters, and every post links to its public URL. Author is the public handle only; app-store reviewer names are omitted.

HOW THE NUMBERS WORK. Snapshots are cumulative. Days before 2026-10-08 are a backfill: they count posts whose post date is on or before that day, using posts found later, so they show what the tracker would have shown had it existed. From 2026-10-08 on, a day counts posts first collected on or before that day. A post tagged with three categories adds one to each, so category counts add up to more than the number of posts. share = category count / that product's posts naming at least one ranked use case. Ties are ordered by category code. The "all products" view pools posts without weighting, so it is dominated by the products with the most posts (Muse, then Instinct); to compare products, use each product's own list.

KNOWN LIMITS. Reddit and Hacker News dates are the UTC calendar date, so a post made in the evening Pacific time can carry the next day's date (any such date later than the collection day is set to the collection day). Keyword search misses posts that do not name the product. The X mirror can rate-limit or miss posts. Reddit RSS returns at most about 100 items per query. App Store feeds stop at about 500 recent reviews. TikTok and Instagram are not covered. Products launched in late September have only days of history. Counts are lower bounds on public chatter, not market share.
